questions.question_text: For which of these angles is $\tan\theta$ undefined?

options.why: $\cos180^{\circ}=-1\ne0$, so $\tan180^{\circ}=0$, not undefined.
$\cos360^{\circ}=1\ne0$, so $\tan360^{\circ}=0$, not undefined.
$\cos45^{\circ}\ne0$, so $\tan45^{\circ}$ is defined.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\theta$ is undefined when $\cos\theta=0$.
At $270^{\circ}$, $P=(0,-1)$, so $\cos270^{\circ}=0$ and $\tan270^{\circ}$ is undefined.

questions.question_text: On the unit circle, $\tan\theta$ equals which of the following?

options.why: Inverted the quotient; $\tan\theta$ is the $y$-over-$x$ gradient, $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
Multiplied the coordinates; the gradient is $y$ divided by $x$.
Subtracted the coordinates; the gradient is $y$ divided by $x$.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\theta$ is the gradient of $OP=\dfrac{y}{x}$, and since $y=\sin\theta$, $x=\cos\theta$:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$
